an4.125:1.1: This is a rare case where a doctrinally significant Sutta has major differences in the editions. In the BJT edition, each of the four divine meditations is told in full, and they correlate one by one with the four realms of rebirth. This reading is supported by the brief note in the commentary, and is followed by Bodhi. However, it is not unproblematic, as it mildly contradicts Visuddhimagga 322.5–12, which says the first three divine meditations can all lead to the first three absorptions (due to the presence of pleasure), but only equanimity can lead to the fourth. The MS and PTS editions, on the other hand, present the release of love in full, leading to rebirth in the host of the Divinity. Then they present the next three divine meditations, abbreviating compassion and rejoicing, and only then list the three higher realms of rebirth. This is not very coherent, and appears to be a corrupted text. Nonetheless, the persistence of such a striking corruption is unusual and noteworthy. I translate following the BJT and commentary. However, given the problems with the text, it would be wise to be cautious before drawing doctrinal conclusions. | Compare, too, the statements of [sn46.54](), which are themselves not entirely clear.
